findings.summary: The change has suggestion reasons draw on the owner's device calendar, but nothing in the spec defines how calendar data gets from the device to the server-side Suggestion. There is no requirement (S.*), operation, entity field or link to ext.device for reading, storing or matching birthdays and anniversaries to ContactRecords.
findings.evidence: entity.Suggestion: "The reason may mention an upcoming birthday or anniversary read from the owner's device calendar". The only device link is evolution.6 affects ext.device. No operation or entity reads ext.device or holds calendar data, and S.webapp.prompts/S.webapp.due say nothing about calendar input.

findings.summary: CalendarAccessToggle is added with an 'off by default' state, but it has no affordance, operation or Account field to persist that consent, and the Settings screen description still lists exactly four components.
findings.evidence: component.CalendarAccessToggle: "Allows reading birthdays and anniversaries from the device calendar; off by default". entity.Account fields are only id, identitySubject, displayName, timeZone and notificationPreferences. screen.settings: "Exactly ProfilePreferences, NotificationPreferences, ExportControls and DeletionControls".

findings.summary: The hook fixture now tests calendar reasons, but its criterion claim does not mention them. SuggestionReason also says reasons include calendar events unconditionally, even though calendar access is off by default.
findings.evidence: hook inputs.fixture: "six due goals yield five ordered cards, incl. calendar reasons" vs C.webapp.prompts.bounded claim: "Six due goals yield exactly five ordered cards. Duplicate jobs must not duplicate prompts or owner reminders". component.SuggestionReason: "including an upcoming birthday or anniversary from the owner's calendar".
